newsitem.title: ESTONIA: ESTONIA-U.S. NRG CONFIDENT OF ENERGY DEAL - AGENCY.
newsitem.headline: ESTONIA-U.S. NRG CONFIDENT OF ENERGY DEAL - AGENCY.

text.p: U.S. power company NRG, part of Northern States Power, is confident its plan for investments into the Estonian electricity sector will go ahead, domestic news agency ETA on Friday quoted NRG's president as saying.
NRG president David Peterson on Thursday met Economy Minister Jaak Leimann as the U.S. group tries to convince the government and parliament to let the plan go ahead.
"Leimann was positive towards the business plan and I received confirmation that the process will continue in Estonia," ETA quoted Peterson as saying.
The plan foresees an investment of $62 million by NRG and the formation of a joint venture to run the two biggest power stations in the country.
Investments to 2005 will total $1.1 billion and prices will rise from 26 sents to 42 sents per kilowatt hour by 2007.
But the plan has run into opposition and a committee of experts recently criticised it on the grounds that it will boost inflation.
